liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (2 reviews): Franklin's Tower and Dancin' in the Streets are described as smooth in the audience recording; China Cat teases during Franklin's Tower make the show extra special for this reviewer [13][18]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The seventh soundcheck take of Stella Blue is singled out as really great [15]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): The pre-show soundcheck Eyes of the World and its jams are strong, with better sound than the concert [10]
- **Supplication** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Supplication as good, and Slipknot! too [11]
- **Help on the Way** (1 review): Reviewer names the Help on the Way > Slipknot! > Franklin's Tower sequence among favorites [12]
- **Dancin' in the Streets** (1 review): Attendee, then 17, was swept away by Dancing in the Street, possibly first hearing the band play it [19]
- **Wharf Rat** (1 review): Wharf Rat gives the show an extra special quality, according to the reviewer [11]

## Setlist highlights

- **Minglewood Blues**: back after 301 archived shows (1901 days) [21]
- **Row Kimmy**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [21]

## The recordings

- **gd76-07-12.sbd.aj.7771.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 36 songs; 218 min; rated 3.73/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1976-07-12.sbd.unknown.10362.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 36 songs; 218 min; rated 2.75/5 by 4 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer's copy of this soundboard has a tape pause near the start [15]
- **gd1976-07-12.150658.sbd.c1stGen.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 30 songs; 230 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1976-07-12.150572.sbd.miller.flac2448**: soundboard; 30 songs; 230 min [4]
- **gd76-07-12.menke.minches.18508.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 23 songs; 162 min; rated 4.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Audience recording quality is admired by reviewer, though acknowledged some find the sound poor; Reviewer says the audience recording sounds great when streamed; Audience recording sounds good but runs slightly fast to the reviewer [12][13][17]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls a very small, intimate theater, perhaps about 1,000 seats, the smallest Dead venue they had seen [19]
- A soundcheck before the show included Dancing in the Street, Stella Blue takes, a Let It Grow jam and Eyes of the World [1]
- Reviewer finds the show unremarkable but says the second set is worth hearing, especially for fans of 1976 [9]
- Reviewer calls the concert solid but typical of 1976 performances [10]
- Reviewer finds it on par with other 1976 shows but somewhat subdued, with no hard-driving rockers [11]
- Called the first official San Francisco show since 10/20/74; the 8/13/75 show was invitation-only [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd76-07-12.sbd.aj.7771.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard - Soundcheck [1]. Also: Soundcheck came from soundboard to master VHS, then DAT, then CD [1]
- **gd1976-07-12.sbd.unknown.10362.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundcheck: SBD>VHS Master>DAT>CDR; Set1: SBD>MR>R>R>R>DAT>CDR; Set2 SBD>MR>DAT>Sonic Solutions>CDR: [2]
- **gd1976-07-12.150658.sbd.c1stGen.miller.flac16**: taped by Dennis Koda; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 13, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell XLII/Dolby B) [3]. Also: First-generation cassettes were supplied by Dennis Koda, with a patch source from Bob Menke and pitch correction settings by Joe B. Jones [3]
- **gd1976-07-12.150572.sbd.miller.flac2448**: taped by Dennis Koda; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  September 13, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master > Cassette (Maxell XLII/Dolby B) [4]. Also: Sony ECM-270 to cassette master to DAT source supplies the patch for U.S. Blues from 6:17 onward [4]
- **gd76-07-12.menke.minches.18508.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Bob Menke; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-270s> Sony TC-152 from front of balcony [6]
